scope: grade 6 NY-6.G.* and NY-6.NS.1 -- additional evidence

added.quote: to introduce nets as two-dimensional representations of polyhedra
Find the surface area (in square units) of the polyhedron.

g6-2023-007.note: Adds the lesson where pyramid nets first appear and the Cool-down where the curriculum tests net-to-surface-area on its own, so the work spans Lessons 13-14 rather than sitting on one activity.

added.lessonTitle: Fractional Lengths in Triangles and Prisms
added.quote: students find the volume of a prism with fractional edge lengths
Find the volume of the box in cubic inches. Show your reasoning.

g6-2023-033.note: Shows that fractional-edge volume is built in Lesson 14 by packing half-inch cubes and tested in the Lesson 15 Cool-down, not only practised in the one activity already cited.

added.quote: Find the areas of at least two of these triangles.

added.lessonTitle: Formula for the Area of a Triangle
added.activity: Applying the Formula for Area of Triangles
added.quote: circle a base measurement that you can use to find the area

g6-2023-037.note: Right-triangle area is reasoned out informally a whole lesson earlier (Lesson 8) before the formula is applied in Lesson 9, so a teacher can start the repair either side of the formula.

added.lessonTitle: Using Diagrams to Find the Number of Groups
added.quote: How many 3/4 s are in 2?

added.activity: Dividing With or Without an Algorithm
added.quote: Calculate at least four quotients. Show your reasoning.

g6-2023-042.note: The same division is set up with diagrams and tested in Lesson 6 and then computed with the algorithm in Lesson 11, so the item is reachable from either end of the unit.

added.quote: What is the volume, in cubic inches, of the rectangular prism?
A storage box has a base that measures 3 inches by 4 inches

g6-2023-045.note: The existing citation is an optional activity; these two are required, and the Cool-down is the only non-optional place that states a prism as a base plus a height, which is the form this item uses.

added.lessonTitle: Fractional Lengths in Triangles and Prisms
added.quote: What is the volume, in cubic inches, of one cube with an edge length
finding the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths

g6-2024-020.note: A cube with a fractional edge length is asked for in exactly two places, the Lesson 14 Cool-down and Lesson 15 Activity 1; the pair is the whole of the curriculum's treatment.

added.quote: different strategies for reasoning about finding the area of regions

added.activity: Finding a Formula for the Area of a Triangle
added.quote: write an expression for the area of any triangle, using b and h

g6-2024-028.note: IM never gives a trapezoid formula, so the item is really Lesson 3's decompose-or-enclose strategies plus Lesson 9's triangle formula, assembled once in Lesson 11 Activity 2.

added.activity: Using Nets to Find Surface Area
added.quote: They use nets to find surface area, applying what they learned earlier
You will draw its net and calculate its surface area.

g6-2024-032.note: Net-to-surface-area is taught in Lesson 14 and practised in Lesson 15 before the Cool-down already cited tests it, so the span is Lessons 14-15 rather than one Cool-down.

added.lessonTitle: Fractional Lengths in Triangles and Prisms
added.quote: Sketch the prism, and find its volume in cubic inches.
Find the volume of the box in cubic inches. Show your reasoning.

g6-2024-035.note: Places the item across the introduce-practise-assess arc of Lessons 14-15 instead of the single Lesson 15 activity.

added.quote: Find the area, in square units, of each shaded region without counting every square
Find the area of the shaded region(s) of each figure.

g6-2024-040.note: Both main activities of the placement lesson ask the item's question; the off-grid one matters most, because the item's flag carries labelled lengths and no grid.

added.quote: A cube has edge length 5 in. Use an exponent to express its volume.
Use an exponent to express its volume.

g6-2024-044.note: The item's two demands are split across Lesson 17: Activity 2 supplies the term perfect cube and Activity 3 plus the Cool-down supply the exponent notation the item asks students to use.

added.quote: How many 1/8 s are in 1 1/4 ?

added.lessonTitle: Using Diagrams to Find the Number of Groups
added.quote: How many groups of 1/2 pound are in 2 3/4 pounds?

g6-2025-006.note: Counting fractional servings in a mixed number starts a lesson earlier with fraction strips, so a teacher can reach the item without the tape diagrams of Lesson 6.

added.quote: surface area of a three-dimensional figure is the total area of all its faces
What kind of polyhedron can be assembled from this net?

g6-2025-013.note: Adds the definition of surface area in Lesson 12 and the Cool-down that tests reading an undimensioned net, widening the entry from Lesson 14 alone to Lessons 12-14.

added.lessonTitle: Formula for the Area of a Triangle
added.activity: Applying the Formula for Area of Triangles
added.quote: circle a base measurement that you can use to find the area
decompose the quadrilateral into parallelograms and triangles to find the area

g6-2025-017.note: The existing citation is optional, and it is the unit's only activity about a non-quadrilateral polygon; these two are required and supply the item's actual moves, one triangle's area and decomposing a polygon into triangles.

added.lessonTitle: Fractional Lengths in Triangles and Prisms
added.quote: students find the volume of a prism with fractional edge lengths
What is the volume, in cubic inches, of the rectangular prism?

g6-2025-034.note: Backs the Cool-down already cited with the two activities that build and practise the same computation, so the entry shows where to reteach rather than only where it is tested.

added.quote: What is the area of the shaded part of the flag?
identify an appropriate pair of base-height measurements to use

g6-2025-036.note: The item is a shaded-part-of-a-figure question on a parallelogram, so it draws on Lesson 6's base-height choice as much as Lesson 11's decomposing, and Lesson 3's Cool-down is where a shaded part is actually tested.

added.quote: to introduce nets as two-dimensional representations of polyhedra

g6-2025-042.note: Pairs the Cool-down already cited with the lesson that introduces pyramid nets and the activity that teaches the calculation, which is what a show-your-work item needs.

added.quote: the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths can be found by multiplying
Two rectangular picture frames have the same area of 45 square inches

g6-2025-043.note: Finding a missing side from a fractional area lives entirely in Lesson 13; the Cool-down is the only place it is tested, and the activity that justifies area as a product of fractional sides is optional.

added.quote: How many 1/2 s are in 2? How many 1/5 s are in 3?

added.quote: Explain or show how you could find 5 ÷ 1/3

g6-2026-009.note: Dividing a number by a unit fraction is counted concretely in Lesson 5 and tested in the Lesson 10 Cool-down, so the entry now spans the concrete and the generalised forms.

added.lessonTitle: Fractional Lengths in Triangles and Prisms
added.quote: students find the volume of a prism with fractional edge lengths
Find the volume of the box in cubic inches. Show your reasoning.

g6-2026-011.note: Adds required evidence either side of the cited activity; the closest textual echo in the curriculum, Lesson 15's Fish Tank, is optional and was left out for that reason.

Find the surface area of your polyhedron. Show your thinking in an organized manner

g6-2026-016.note: Shows that a triangular-prism net is worked in Lesson 14 and Lesson 15 before the Cool-down already cited assesses it, which is more useful than the Cool-down alone.

added.quote: Find four other numbers that are perfect cubes and two numbers that are not
Use an exponent to express its volume.

g6-2026-022.note: Perfect cubes and exponent notation are introduced, practised and tested inside Lesson 17 alone; no other lesson in the unit touches this item, which is worth knowing before skipping the lesson.

added.quote: The triangle covers half of the region of each parallelogram.

g6-2026-029.note: The halving the item's diagram invites is established in the Lesson 8 Warm-up, and the base-height choice the 10 m distractor punishes is tested in the Lesson 9 Cool-down.

added.lessonTitle: Fractional Lengths in Triangles and Prisms
added.quote: Sketch the prism, and find its volume in cubic inches.
Describe a different way to find the volume of the box.

g6-2026-035.note: Widens the shared Lesson 15 activity with the lesson that builds fractional-edge volume and the Cool-down that asks for a second method, which is what a three-mixed-number product rewards.

added.quote: different strategies for reasoning about finding the area of regions
What is the area of the shaded part of the flag?

g6-2026-043.note: A right trapezoid is a rectangle plus a right triangle, which is Lesson 3's decompose-or-enclose work; that Cool-down is the closest the unit comes to assessing it, since Lesson 11 has no area Cool-down.
